statement: Morgan Stanley finds no sign the memory supply shortage is easing and flags the possibility that shortages intensify in 2027 and 2028.
why: If the memory squeeze runs years rather than quarters, it becomes a structural ceiling on how many AI accelerators and servers can be built, not a passing price spike.

impact.mechanism: A shortage expected to persist or intensify through 2027-2028 keeps memory allocation the binding constraint on accelerator and AI-server output.

evidence.source: BigGo Finance — "DRAM Spot Prices Hit Record Highs; 'Q3 Contract Prices to Surge Another 25%+'"
evidence.excerpt: no signs that the memory supply shortage is easing

evidence.source: BigGo Finance — "DRAM Spot Prices Hit Record Highs; 'Q3 Contract Prices to Surge Another 25%+'"
evidence.excerpt: possibility that supply shortages could intensify in 2027 and 2028

confidence.basis: Qualitative forward-looking analyst view relayed by one secondary outlet; capped at medium under the secondary-evidence rule.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: magnitude 1 -> 2; sources: BigGo Finance — "DRAM Spot Prices Hit Record Highs; 'Q3 Contract Prices to Surge Another 25%+'", DIGITIMES — "Memory shortage to worsen in 2027 as AI inference strains supply"
